title: Overloaded defenders
outcomes: Finds a piece that defends two things and the move that exploits it
Lists every job of a defender before attacking it
Says why a second defender or a shared line cancels the idea

steps.text: A piece with **two jobs** can be beaten. If one defender guards two targets, attack one: when it answers there, the other is left alone. This is an *overloaded defender*. Ask: which piece guards two things, and can it keep both?

Not every piece with two jobs is overloaded. **List all its jobs.** Then ask whether they are both needed at once, and whether one move of the defender or a block can serve both. Only a defender forced to choose is overloaded.

steps.title: A second defender of the rook
steps.prompt: The white king stands on b1 and also defends a2.

steps.text: **When it holds:** both jobs are needed now and one move cannot do both; your move forces a capture or check. **When it fails:** another piece shares a job, or the jobs lie on one line. As a rule of thumb, count the defenders of each target, not just the one you attack.

steps.prompt: When you thought a piece was overloaded, did you list every job it had and every other defender?
